sentences.en: As protests and unrest over racial justice and policing continue to erupt across the U.S.
sentences.zh: 随着围绕种族正义和警务的抗议与动荡在美国各地持续爆发。

sentences.en: These radicals are not content with marching in the streets.
sentences.zh: 这些激进分子并不满足于在街头游行。

sentences.en: These are the people who will be in charge of your future and the future of your children.
sentences.zh: 这些人将掌管你们的未来，以及你们孩子的未来。

sentences.en: Speaker after speaker at the Republican
sentences.zh: 本周在共和党

sentences.en: National Convention this week.
sentences.zh: 全国代表大会上，演讲者一个接一个地发言。

sentences.en: When we don't have basic safety and security in our communities, we'll never be free to build a brighter future for ourselves, for our children, or for our country.
sentences.zh: 当我们社区缺乏基本的安全保障时，我们就永远无法为自己、为我们的孩子、为我们的国家建设一个更美好的未来。

sentences.en: Have put them at the center of their appeal to a key group of voters.
sentences.zh: 将他们置于其吸引关键选民群体的核心位置。

sentences.en: They're not satisfied with spreading the chaos and violence into our communities.
sentences.zh: 他们并不满足于将混乱和暴力蔓延到我们的社区。

sentences.en: They want to abolish the suburbs altogether.
sentences.zh: 他们想要彻底废除郊区。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Emily Badger on the power of the suburban vote.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事艾米丽·巴杰将探讨郊区选票的力量。

sentences.en: If you're a traditional Democrat who's become disillusioned with how radical your party has become, then stand with us.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一位对本党激进程度感到失望的传统民主党人，那就站在我们这边。

sentences.en: You are most welcome.
sentences.zh: 我们非常欢迎你。

sentences.en: And the Republican Party's pitch to win it back.
sentences.zh: 以及共和党为赢回这些选票所做的努力。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, August 26th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月26日，星期三。

sentences.en: Emily, you have been thinking a lot about the upcoming election and how suburban America fits into it.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，你一直在深入思考即将到来的选举，以及郊区美国在其中扮演的角色。

sentences.en: Why are we hearing so much about that demographic right now at the Republican National
sentences.zh: 为什么我们现在在共和党全国

sentences.en: Convention?
sentences.zh: 代表大会上听到这么多关于这一人口群体的讨论？

sentences.en: Because it feels like such a specific and explicit form of outreach.
sentences.zh: 因为这感觉像是一种非常具体且明确的拉票方式。

sentences.en: So suburban voters have really been the focal point of presidential elections going all the way back to the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 郊区选民实际上从20世纪60年代开始就一直是总统选举的焦点。

sentences.en: We have seen this pattern over time where it's increasingly clear that voters in cities are going to vote Democratic, rural voters are going to vote Republican.
sentences.zh: 我们观察到一种长期模式，即城市选民越来越倾向于投票给民主党，而农村选民则倾向于投票给共和党，这一点日益清晰。

sentences.en: All of the suspense, the whole ballgame is in the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 所有的悬念，整个博弈的关键都在郊区。

sentences.en: And so, you know, these are the voters that we have been fighting over for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这些就是我们长期以来一直在争夺的选民。

sentences.en: And so it's not surprising that coming down to the last couple months of this election, that these are the voters that we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这次选举进入最后几个月时，我们讨论这些选民也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So when we think about purple America, swing America, we're really talking about the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们想到“紫色美国”、摇摆州时，我们实际上指的就是郊区。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Well, where does that story of politics and the suburbs start?
sentences.zh: 那么，政治与郊区的故事是从哪里开始的呢？

sentences.en: Well, I have been thinking a lot this year about 1968 in particular.
sentences.zh: 嗯，今年我一直在思考1968年，特别是那一年。

sentences.en: 1968 was this really pivotal year for a lot of reasons in American politics.
sentences.zh: 1968年在美国政治中是一个非常关键的年份，原因有很多。

sentences.en: We think about what was happening in the country at that moment.
sentences.zh: 我们回想一下当时国家正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 晚上好。

sentences.en: The Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King,
sentences.zh: 马丁·路德·金博士牧师，

sentences.en: 39 years old and a Nobel Peace Prize winner, and the leader of the nonviolent civil rights movement in the United States was assassinated in Memphis tonight.
sentences.zh: 39岁，诺贝尔和平奖得主，美国非暴力民权运动的领袖，今晚在孟菲斯遇刺身亡。

sentences.en: Martin Luther King gets assassinated in the first week of April.
sentences.zh: 马丁·路德·金在4月的第一周被暗杀。

sentences.en: Police report that the murder has touched off sporadic acts of violence in a Negro section of the city.
sentences.zh: 警方报告称，这起谋杀案在该市的黑人区引发了零星的暴力行为。

sentences.en: There is a wave of civil unrest that happens not just in one or two cities, but in more than a hundred cities across the country.
sentences.zh: 一场民事动荡浪潮不仅发生在一两个城市，而是席卷了全国一百多个城市。

sentences.en: Police report having made more than 600 arrests with over half these still in custody.
sentences.zh: 警方报告称已逮捕了600多人，其中半数以上仍被拘留。

sentences.en: Three deaths have been reported so far.
sentences.zh: 目前已报告有三人死亡。

sentences.en: Some of the worst trouble of the day occurred in Washington, D.C., the very heart of the nation.
sentences.zh: 当天最严重的骚乱发生在国家的心脏地带——华盛顿特区。

sentences.en: In some Negro ghettos, there was looting, arson, and bloodshed during the night.
sentences.zh: 在一些黑人贫民窟，夜间发生了抢劫、纵火和流血事件。

sentences.en: 4,000 National Guard and federal troops are in this uneasy town tonight.
sentences.zh: 今晚有4000名国民警卫队和联邦军队驻扎在这个不安的城镇。

sentences.en: To shoot to kill any arsonist or anyone with a Molotov cocktail in their hand in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 在芝加哥，下令射杀任何纵火犯或任何手持莫洛托夫鸡尾酒的人。

sentences.en: There's some police here.
sentences.zh: 这里有一些警察。

sentences.en: They're shooting around here.
sentences.zh: 他们正在这附近开枪。

sentences.en: The 15th and Kesey.
sentences.zh: 第15街和凯西街。

sentences.en: And to issue a police order to shoot the main or crippled anyone looting.
sentences.zh: 并下达警察命令，射杀任何抢劫者，无论其是否受伤。

sentences.en: Well, I'm saddened and angered by what has happened.
sentences.zh: 我为所发生的一切感到悲伤和愤怒。

sentences.en: We've marked the death of a man of peace, a man of goodwill with colossal violence, destruction, and death.
sentences.zh: 我们用巨大的暴力、破坏和死亡，纪念了一位和平之士、一位善意之人的离世。

sentences.en: I would insist that law and order must prevail.
sentences.zh: 我坚持认为法律和秩序必须占上风。

sentences.en: And I'm, of course, angered by the needless, silly, stupid destruction that I've seen in both Washington and Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 当然，我也对我在华盛顿和巴尔的摩所看到的那些毫无必要、愚蠢至极的破坏感到愤怒。

sentences.en: I never believed this could happen in our nation's capital or in my city.
sentences.zh: 我从未相信这会发生在我们的国家首都或我的城市。

sentences.en: Out of this moment, there really emerges, you know, this very strong backlash, particularly among white middle-class suburban voters, against all of this unrest and against
sentences.zh: 在这一时刻，确实出现了一种非常强烈的反弹，特别是在白人中产阶级郊区选民中，他们反对所有这些动荡，反对

sentences.en: the sense that there's crime and there's violence and we're fed up with it.
sentences.zh: 那种认为犯罪和暴力横行、我们对此感到厌倦的情绪。

sentences.en: We just want order.
sentences.zh: 我们只想要秩序。

sentences.en: And as a reminder, what do the suburbs in America look like at this point in the 1960s?
sentences.zh: 作为提醒，20世纪60年代的美国郊区是什么样子的？

sentences.en: Because my sense is that the concept of a suburb, right, these kind of planned communities on the edges
sentences.zh: 因为我的感觉是，郊区的概念，对吧，这些在城市边缘的规划社区，

sentences.en: of cities, tidy yards, white picket fences, that that's kind of new in this moment.
sentences.zh: 整洁的院子，白色的栅栏，在当时似乎是新鲜事物。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we see this huge explosion of suburbia after World War II.
sentences.zh: 我们在二战后看到了郊区化的巨大爆发。

sentences.en: At last, the Bryants have all the space they need.
sentences.zh: 终于，布莱恩特一家拥有了他们所需的所有空间。

sentences.en: And the people who are able to move to suburbia in that moment are not sort of representative of the entire American population.
sentences.zh: 而在当时能够搬到郊区的人，并不代表整个美国人口。

sentences.en: It's very specific groups of people who get to go.
sentences.zh: 只有非常特定的群体才能搬进去。

sentences.en: The home they've always dreamed of, the happiest investment they have ever made.
sentences.zh: 他们梦寐以求的家，他们做过的最幸福的投资。

sentences.en: So it's primarily white residents who get to go.
sentences.zh: 所以主要是白人居民才能搬进去。

sentences.en: The separate dining room is another feature that delights Margaret Bryant in her new home, for it permits her to enjoy her guests while entertaining graciously.
sentences.zh: 独立的餐厅是玛格丽特·布莱恩特新家中的另一个特色，令她欣喜不已，因为它让她在优雅地招待客人的同时也能享受其中。

sentences.en: It's primarily middle-class and upper-income white residents who get to go.
sentences.zh: 主要是中产阶级和高收入的白人居民才能搬进去。

sentences.en: The patio, easily reached through sliding glass doors, provides an outdoor living room ideal for separate activities.
sentences.zh: 通过滑动玻璃门可以轻松到达的露台，提供了一个理想的户外起居室，适合进行各种活动。

sentences.en: So in this moment in the 1960s, when we talk about the suburbs, they are racially exclusionary by design.
sentences.zh: 所以在20世纪60年代的这个时刻，当我们谈论郊区时，它们在设计上就是种族排外的。

sentences.en: It is intentional that African Americans cannot move out there at that point.
sentences.zh: 非裔美国人在当时无法搬到那里是蓄意的。

sentences.en: This is how American families are living in their new homes.
sentences.zh: 这就是美国家庭在新家中的生活方式。

sentences.en: And so the civil rights movement begins to threaten that sense of exclusion because now we're talking about busing.
sentences.zh: 因此，民权运动开始威胁到那种排他感，因为现在我们谈论的是校车接送问题。

sentences.en: Now we're talking about fair housing.
sentences.zh: 现在我们谈论的是公平住房。

sentences.en: We're talking about whether or not it's fair for homeowners to be able to say, I don't want to have Black neighbors, for realtors to say,
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是房主是否有权说“我不想要黑人邻居”，房地产经纪人是否有权说，

sentences.en: I don't want to work with Black homebuyers.
sentences.zh: “我不想与黑人购房者合作”，这是否公平。

sentences.en: And at this same moment, we also see the rise of a number of politicians who are themselves sort of suburban politicians who figure out how to give voice to that anxiety,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我们也看到了一批政客的崛起，他们本身就是某种郊区政客，他们找到了如何表达这种焦虑的方法，

sentences.en: how to take this growing group of the electorate who live in the suburbs
sentences.zh: 如何将这群不断壮大的郊区选民

sentences.en: and turn them into a voting bloc where you are speaking directly to their concerns about their own suburban security.
sentences.zh: 转化为一个投票集团，直接回应他们对自身郊区安全的担忧。

sentences.en: And of course, 1968 is a presidential election year.
sentences.zh: 当然，1968年是总统选举年。

sentences.en: So how do we see all of that play out?
sentences.zh: 那么我们是如何看到这一切上演的呢？

sentences.en: In recent years, crime in this country has grown nine times as fast as population.
sentences.zh: 近年来，我国的犯罪率增长速度是人口增长速度的九倍。

sentences.en: We see Richard Nixon increasingly make law and order a centerpiece of his stump speeches.
sentences.zh: 我们看到理查德·尼克松越来越多地将“法律与秩序”作为他竞选演讲的核心。

sentences.en: We owe it to the decent and law-abiding citizens of America to take the offensive against the criminal forces that threaten their peace and their security.
sentences.zh: 我们有责任为美国体面和守法的公民挺身而出，打击威胁他们和平与安全的犯罪势力。

sentences.en: And he is talking more and more about crime.
sentences.zh: 他越来越多地谈论犯罪问题。

sentences.en: I pledge to you, the wave of crime is not going to be the wave of the future in America.
sentences.zh: 我向你们保证，犯罪浪潮不会成为美国未来的浪潮。

sentences.en: Spending more money on the police.
sentences.zh: 在警察身上投入更多资金。

sentences.en: Dissent is a necessary ingredient of change.
sentences.zh: 异议是变革的必要成分。

sentences.en: But in a system of government that provides for peaceful change, there is no cause that justifies resort to violence.
sentences.zh: 但在一个提供和平变革的政府体制中，没有任何理由诉诸暴力。

sentences.en: Sort of speaking to these issues about, you know, how you should be able to protect what you have earned as a kind of hardworking American who's bought your way into the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上是在谈论这些问题，即作为一个辛苦工作的美国人，你如何能够保护你通过努力赚取并买下郊区房产所获得的一切。

sentences.en: Let us recognize that the first civil right of every American is to be free from domestic violence.
sentences.zh: 让我们认识到，每个美国人的第一项公民权利就是免受家庭暴力的侵害。

sentences.en: You should be able to protect that without fear that all of this chaos that's happening in cities is going to come to your doorstep.
sentences.zh: 你应该能够保护这一点，而不必担心城市中发生的所有这些混乱会蔓延到你的家门口。

sentences.en: So I pledge to you, we shall have order in the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以我向你们保证，我们将在美国实现秩序。

sentences.en: And then we get to the Republican National Convention in 1968 in Miami,
sentences.zh: 然后我们来到了1968年在迈阿密举行的共和党全国代表大会，

sentences.en: which is actually taking place at a moment when there is unrest happening in the Liberty City neighborhood of Miami.
sentences.zh: 这实际上发生在一个动荡不安的时刻，当时迈阿密的自由城社区正在发生骚乱。

sentences.en: We make history tonight, not for ourselves, but for the Asians.
sentences.zh: 我们今晚创造了历史，不是为了我们自己，而是为了美国人民。

sentences.en: And Richard Nixon gives this speech where he talks about...
sentences.zh: 理查德·尼克松发表了演讲，他谈到了……

sentences.en: As we look at America, we see cities enveloped in smoke and flame.
sentences.zh: 当我们审视美国时，我们看到城市笼罩在烟雾和火焰中。

sentences.en: We hear sirens in the night.
sentences.zh: 我们在深夜听到警笛声。

sentences.en: Cities enveloped in smoke and flame.
sentences.zh: 城市笼罩在烟雾和火焰中。

sentences.en: We see Americans hating each other, fighting each other, killing each other at home.
sentences.zh: 我们看到美国人在国内互相仇恨、互相争斗、互相残杀。

sentences.en: And he devotes a long passage to talking about law and order.
sentences.zh: 他用了很长的篇幅来谈论法律和秩序。

sentences.en: The American Revolution was and is dedicated to progress, but our founders recognized that the first requisite of progress is order.
sentences.zh: 美国革命致力于进步，但我们的开国元勋们认识到，进步的首要前提是秩序。

sentences.en: And one of the things that's most striking to me about that speech is he even says...
sentences.zh: 那次演讲中最让我印象深刻的一点是，他甚至说……

sentences.en: And to those who say that law and order is the code word for racism, there and here is the reply.
sentences.zh: 对于那些说“法律与秩序”是种族主义代号的人，这就是回答。

sentences.en: This emphasis on law and order is not raciSt.
sentences.zh: 这种对法律与秩序的强调并非种族主义。

sentences.en: Our goal is justice.
sentences.zh: 我们的目标是正义。

sentences.en: Justice for every American.
sentences.zh: 为每一位美国人伸张正义。

sentences.en: If we are to have respect for law in America, we must have laws that deserve respect.
sentences.zh: 如果我们要在美国尊重法律，我们就必须拥有值得尊重的法律。

sentences.en: Just as we cannot have progress without order, we cannot have order without progress.
sentences.zh: 正如我们不能没有秩序就取得进步一样，没有进步我们也无法拥有秩序。

sentences.en: And so as we commit to order tonight, let us commit to progress.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们今晚致力于秩序时，让我们也致力于进步。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's giving white suburbanites permission to be upset, to be fearful.
sentences.zh: 他允许白人郊区居民感到不安和恐惧。

sentences.en: He's giving them not only permission, but he's giving them a language to talk about their grievances that doesn't sound like the language of racism.
sentences.zh: 他不仅给予了他们许可，还给了他们一种谈论不满的语言，听起来不像种族主义的语言。

sentences.en: It sounds instead like the language of property values and quality schools and security and prosperity.
sentences.zh: 相反，它听起来像是关于房产价值、优质学校、安全和繁荣的语言。

sentences.en: For the past five years, we have been deluged by government programs for the unemployed, programs for the cities, programs for the poor.
sentences.zh: 在过去的五年里，我们被政府为失业者提供的项目、为城市提供的项目、为穷人提供的项目所淹没。

sentences.en: And we have reaped from these programs an ugly harvest of frustration, violence and failure across the land.
sentences.zh: 而我们从这些项目中收获的，是全国范围内挫折、暴力和失败的丑陋果实。

sentences.en: And he also sort of says that he is speaking to...
sentences.zh: 他还表示他是在为……说话。

sentences.en: It is a quiet voice in the tumult of the shouting.
sentences.zh: 这是喧嚣中的一个安静的声音。

sentences.en: It is the voice of the great majority of Americans, the forgotten Americans, the non-shouters, the non-demonstrators.
sentences.zh: 这是绝大多数美国人的声音，是被遗忘的美国人，是不喧哗者，是不示威者。

sentences.en: The forgotten and the silent Americans who are not demonstrating.
sentences.zh: 那些没有参加示威的被遗忘的沉默的美国人。

sentences.en: Those people who are sort of silently watching everything that's happening in America from their quiet neighborhoods in the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 那些在郊区安静的社区里默默注视着美国发生的一切的人。

sentences.en: Those are the people who he wants to speak to.
sentences.zh: 这些人就是他想要对话的对象。

sentences.en: They're not racist or sick.
sentences.zh: 他们不是种族主义者，也不是病态的。

sentences.en: They're not guilty of the crime that plagues the land.
sentences.zh: 他们没有犯下困扰这片土地的罪行。

sentences.en: They are black and they are white.
sentences.zh: 他们有黑人，也有白人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is where we get that phrase that Nixon uses in 1968.
sentences.zh: 这就是尼克松在1968年使用的那个短语的由来。

sentences.en: And you've begun to hint at it, the silent majority.
sentences.zh: 你已经开始暗示它了，即“沉默的大多数”。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Emily, what is our understanding of the role that this strategy ultimately played in that election?
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，我们如何理解这一策略在当年的选举中最终发挥的作用？

sentences.en: So 1968 is this year when suburban voters deliver the presidency to Richard Nixon.
sentences.zh: 1968年是郊区选民将理查德·尼克松送上总统宝座的一年。

sentences.en: And suburban voters and their preferences become central to American politics.
sentences.zh: 郊区选民及其偏好成为美国政治的核心。

sentences.en: And they have largely been central to presidential elections ever since then.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，他们基本上一直是总统选举的核心。

sentences.en: So how do we see that play out in the years that follow?
sentences.zh: 那么我们如何看待这一现象在随后的几年里如何演变？

sentences.en: So after 1968, as it becomes clear that suburban voters are the swing voters, the pivotal voters in American elections,
sentences.zh: 1968年之后，随着郊区选民成为摇摆选民、美国选举中的关键选民这一点变得清晰，

sentences.en: their concerns come to dominate not just what the Republican Party is doing, but also what the Democratic Party is doing.
sentences.zh: 他们的关切不仅开始主导共和党的行动，也开始主导民主党的行动。

sentences.en: And so these are themes that we hear from Ronald Reagan.
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是我们从罗纳德·里根那里听到的主题。

sentences.en: Crime is an American epidemic.
sentences.zh: 犯罪是一种美国流行病。

sentences.en: It takes the lives of 25,000 Americans.
sentences.zh: 它夺去了25,000名美国人的生命。

sentences.en: It touches nearly one-third of American households.
sentences.zh: 它影响了近三分之一的美国家庭。

sentences.en: There are also themes that we hear from Bill Clinton.
sentences.zh: 我们从比尔·克林顿那里也听到了类似的主题。

sentences.en: Let us roll up our sleeves to roll back this awful tide of violence and reduce crime in our country.
sentences.zh: 让我们撸起袖子，去扭转这股可怕的暴力浪潮，减少我国的犯罪。

sentences.en: We have the tools now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在已经有了工具。

sentences.en: Let us get about the business of using them.
sentences.zh: 让我们着手使用它们吧。

sentences.en: And this carries us all the way through to 2016 when Donald Trump comes on the scene.
sentences.zh: 这一直延续到2016年唐纳德·特朗普登场。

sentences.en: We have a situation where we have our inner cities, African-Americans, Hispanics, are living in hell because it's so dangerous.
sentences.zh: 我们现在的处境是，我们的内城区，非裔美国人、拉美裔，生活在水深火热之中，因为那里太危险了。

sentences.en: You walk down the street, you get shot.
sentences.zh: 走在街上，你就会被枪击。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Emily, I feel like when most people think about the 2016 campaign, they probably think about Trump's language and his message around immigration.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，我觉得当大多数人想到2016年竞选时，他们可能首先想到的是特朗普的言论和他关于移民的信息。

sentences.en: But it wasn't just limited to that.
sentences.zh: 但这并不局限于此。

sentences.en: I covered the 2016 Republican National Convention, and I remember that Trump...
sentences.zh: 我报道了2016年共和党全国代表大会，我记得特朗普……

sentences.en: I have a message to every last person threatening the peace on our streets.
sentences.zh: 我要向每一个威胁我们街道和平的人传达一个信息。

sentences.en: ...explicitly modeled his message that year on Richard Nixon's message from 1968, and that he was not bashful about it.
sentences.zh: ……那一年明确地以理查德·尼克松1968年的信息为蓝本，而且他对此毫不避讳。

sentences.en: When I take the oath of office next year, I will restore law and order to our country.
sentences.zh: 明年我宣誓就职时，我将恢复我国的法律与秩序。

sentences.en: I actually wrote a story about this, and around that time, Trump said, and I'm going to quote from him,
sentences.zh: 我当时确实写过一篇关于此事的报道，在那段时间里，特朗普曾说——我引用他的话——

sentences.en: I think what Nixon understood is that when the world is falling apart, people want a strong leader whose highest priority is protecting America firSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为尼克松明白的是，当世界分崩离析时，人们需要一位强有力的领导人，其最高优先级是保护美国优先。

sentences.en: The 60s were bad, really bad, and it's really bad now.
sentences.zh: 60年代很糟糕，非常糟糕，而现在也真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: Americans feel like it's chaos again.
sentences.zh: 美国人觉得这又是一片混乱。

sentences.en: I mean, he picked up these themes in 2016 in such a forceful way that almost felt kind of discordant with what was going on around us in America at the time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他在2016年以一种极其强有力的方式拾起了这些主题，这与当时美国周围发生的事情显得有些不协调。

sentences.en: You look at Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 看看巴尔的摩。

sentences.en: You look at the violence that's taking place in the inner cities, Chicago.
sentences.zh: 看看内城区正在发生的暴力事件，比如芝加哥。

sentences.en: You take a look at Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 再看看华盛顿特区。

sentences.en: We have an increase in murder.
sentences.zh: 我们的谋杀案在增加。

sentences.en: So he was speaking a lot about, you know, these tremendous crime spikes.
sentences.zh: 所以他谈论了很多关于，你知道的，这些巨大的犯罪激增。

sentences.en: There were some cities where crime was increasing at the time, but we were still in one of the lowest crime eras that we've had in decades in America.
sentences.zh: 当时确实有一些城市的犯罪率在上升，但我们仍然处于美国几十年来犯罪率最低的时期之一。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But for too many of our citizens, a different reality exists.
sentences.zh: 但对于我们太多的公民来说，存在着另一种现实。

sentences.en: But it remains true at the same time that even as crime has fallen precipitously in America, fears about crime and law and order have always remained really strong for many people.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，即便美国的犯罪率急剧下降，对于许多人来说，对犯罪以及法律与秩序的恐惧始终非常强烈，这一点依然是真的。

sentences.en: And we consistently see in polling across time that Americans believe that crime is increasing even when it's declining, that they believe that it is worse than it really is.
sentences.zh: 我们始终在民调中看到，美国人认为犯罪率在上升，即使它在下降；他们认为情况比实际更糟。

sentences.en: So it is possible for Trump to tap into those fears, I think, even in a moment where it looks like crime is at a historic low.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，即使在犯罪率看起来处于历史低点的时候，特朗普也有可能利用这些恐惧。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And Emily, what do we know about how this message in 2016 landed in the suburbs?
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，我们对2016年这一信息在郊区的反响了解多少？

sentences.en: So the 2016 election is, again, most closely fought in the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 所以2016年的选举，再次在郊区展开了最激烈的争夺。

sentences.en: Trump gets wiped out in big cities and in the densest places in America.
sentences.zh: 特朗普在大城市和美国人口最稠密的地方惨败。

sentences.en: Hillary Clinton fares even worse in rural America than Barack Obama did.
sentences.zh: 希拉里·克林顿在农村地区的表现甚至比巴拉克·奥巴马还要差。

sentences.en: And then in these in-between places in the suburbs,
sentences.zh: 然后在这些中间地带的郊区，

sentences.en: it is incredibly closely contested to the point where whether or not Trump won the suburbs is heavily dependent on exactly how you define them.
sentences.zh: 竞争极其激烈，以至于特朗普是否赢得了郊区，很大程度上取决于你如何定义它们。

sentences.en: And so this launches us into the Trump administration itself when white college-educated suburban women in these highly educated suburban districts wind up being pivotal to the backlash against Trump.
sentences.zh: 这把我们带入了特朗普政府时期，当时这些受过高等教育的郊区选区中的白人大学女性，最终成为了反对特朗普浪潮的关键。

sentences.en: They wind up giving Democrats control of the House of Representatives in the 2018 midterMs.
sentences.zh: 她们最终在2018年中期选举中让民主党获得了众议院的控制权。

sentences.en: So that would seem to set up the suburban white woman voter as an essential, maybe the essential demographic for the 2020 presidential race.
sentences.zh: 这似乎将郊区白人女性选民定位为2020年总统大选的关键，甚至是最关键的人口群体。

sentences.en: It's clear in 2018 that as Trump has lost a lot of support, particularly among white women, among white suburban women, that if he is going to gain ground in the 2020 election,
sentences.zh: 2018年很清楚，随着特朗普失去了很多支持，特别是在白人女性、白人郊区女性中，如果他想在2020年大选中获得优势，

sentences.en: he's going to need to win some of those women back.
sentences.zh: 他需要赢回其中一些女性的支持。

sentences.en: So we see that coming.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到了这一点。

sentences.en: We know that that's going to be an issue in 2020.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这将是2020年的一个议题。

sentences.en: But I think what we don't see coming is that we're going to be back in this moment a couple months before the 2020 election,
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们没预料到的是，在2020年大选前几个月，我们又回到了这个时刻，

sentences.en: where we are again talking about racial unrest in the United States.
sentences.zh: 我们再次谈论美国境内的种族动荡。

sentences.en: Just like in 1968.
sentences.zh: 就像1968年一样。

sentences.en: I think if you're Donald Trump, you look at this moment and that's what you think.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你是唐纳德·特朗普，你看着这一刻，你就会这么想。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，免费获取30天的访问权限。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 晚上好。

sentences.en: I'm Ronna McDaniel, chairwoman of the Republican National Committee.
sentences.zh: 我是罗娜·麦克丹尼尔，共和党全国委员会主席。

sentences.en: And on behalf of everyone in our party and President Trump, thank you for tuning in as we kick off this historic convention.
sentences.zh: 我代表我们党内的每一个人和特朗普总统，感谢你们收看我们这场历史性大会的开幕。

sentences.en: So, you know, Emily, I was watching the Republican National Convention on the opening night and having heard you now explain the messaging from the RNC in 1968,
sentences.zh: 所以，艾米丽，我在开幕当晚观看了共和党全国代表大会，现在听你解释了1968年共和党全国委员会的信息传递，

sentences.en: it's sort of astonishing just how much the messaging from the RNC in 2020 hits the same notes.
sentences.zh: 2020年共和党全国委员会的信息传递在很大程度上与当年的基调如出一辙，这真是令人震惊。

sentences.en: There are these exact same themes and even identical language about...
sentences.zh: 有着完全相同的主题，甚至连用词都一模一样，关于……

sentences.en: It's almost like this election is shaping up to be church, work and school versus rioting, looting and vandalism.
sentences.zh: 这简直就像是这次选举正在演变成“教堂、工作和学校”对阵“骚乱、抢劫和破坏”。

sentences.en: Cities on fire, looting, vandalism, we don't have law and order, we need to restore law and order, and it's coming from...
sentences.zh: 城市在燃烧，抢劫，破坏，我们没有法律与秩序，我们需要恢复法律与秩序，而这来自……

sentences.en: Law and order is on the ballot.
sentences.zh: 法律与秩序就在选票上。

sentences.en: Speaker...
sentences.zh: 议长……

sentences.en: They call it defunding, and it's a danger to our cities, our neighborhoods and our children.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为削减经费，这对我们的城市、我们的社区和我们的孩子来说是一种危险。

sentences.en: After Speaker...
sentences.zh: 在议长之后……

sentences.en: Look at what's happening in American cities.
sentences.zh: 看看美国城市正在发生什么。

sentences.en: Cities all run by Democrats.
sentences.zh: 所有城市都由民主党人管理。

sentences.en: Crime, violence, and mob rule.
sentences.zh: 犯罪、暴力和暴民统治。

sentences.en: After Speaker, it's really a theme that they return to throughout the night, and it's embedded in this idea that this is what will happen in a Democratic administration.
sentences.zh: 在议长之后，这确实是他们整晚反复提到的一个主题，它植根于这样一种观念：这就是民主党政府下会发生的事情。

sentences.en: We're seeing all of this chaos in cities that are run by Democratic mayors that have long been strongholds of Democratic politicians.
sentences.zh: 我们看到所有这些混乱都发生在由民主党市长管理的城市，这些城市长期以来一直是民主党政客的据点。

sentences.en: Just take a look at California.
sentences.zh: 看看加利福尼亚州就知道了。

sentences.en: It is a place of immense wealth.
sentences.zh: 那是一个拥有巨大财富的地方。

sentences.en: Immeasurable innovation.
sentences.zh: 不可估量的创新。

sentences.en: An immaculate environment.
sentences.zh: 完美的环境。

sentences.en: And the Democrats turned it into a land of discarded heroin needles in parks, riots in streets, and blackouts in homes.
sentences.zh: 而民主党人把它变成了一个公园里丢弃着海洛因针头、街头发生骚乱、家中停电的土地。

sentences.en: And if we give Democrats control of the entire country, this is what you can expect in your community where you live, too.
sentences.zh: 如果我们让民主党人控制整个国家，这就是你所居住的社区也可能面临的情况。

sentences.en: And it felt like the sort of ultimate example of this was this couple from St. Louis who were given a prime speaking spot on the first night of the Republican convention.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是这种叙事的终极例证，就是这对来自圣路易斯的夫妇，他们在共和党大会的第一晚获得了黄金演讲时段。

sentences.en: This is the couple who back in June drew a lot of attention when images surfaced of them standing in the front of their mansion,
sentences.zh: 这就是那对在六月份引起广泛关注的夫妇，当时有照片显示他们站在自家豪宅前，

sentences.en: pointing guns at protesters as those protesters walked in front of the couple's house on their way to a protest in front of the local mayor's house.
sentences.zh: 用枪指着抗议者，当时那些抗议者正走在他们家门前，前往当地市长家门前进行抗议。

sentences.en: Yeah, so this was a segment and a pair of speakers who I don't think we could have expected to see in any prior Republican National Convention.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个环节，也是一对我们认为在任何之前的共和党全国代表大会上都无法预见的演讲者。

sentences.en: We have this couple.
sentences.zh: 我们有这对夫妇。

sentences.en: Good evening, America.
sentences.zh: 晚上好，美国。

sentences.en: Mark and Matricia McCloskey.
sentences.zh: 马克和帕特里夏·麦克洛斯基。

sentences.en: We are Mark and Patty McCloskey.
sentences.zh: 我们是马克和帕蒂·麦克洛斯基。

sentences.en: We're speaking to you tonight from St. Louis, Missouri, where just weeks ago you may have seen us defending our home as a mob of protesters descended on our neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 我们今晚从密苏里州圣路易斯向你们讲话，就在几周前，你们可能看到我们保卫家园，当时一群抗议者涌入了我们的社区。

sentences.en: And they live on a gated, very upscale street in St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 他们住在圣路易斯一个有门禁、非常高档的街道上。

sentences.en: It's technically inside the city, but has very much sort of the trappings of suburbia.
sentences.zh: 从技术上讲，它在城市内部，但非常有郊区的特征。

sentences.en: And they're speaking to us from what looks like a couch in their living room or their sitting room.
sentences.zh: 他们正从看起来像是客厅或起居室的沙发上对我们讲话。

sentences.en: And they're both wearing blazers.
sentences.zh: 他们都穿着西装外套。

sentences.en: Not a single person in the out-of-control mob you saw at our house was charged with a crime.
sentences.zh: 你们在我们家看到的失控暴民中，没有一个人被指控犯罪。

sentences.en: But you know who was?
sentences.zh: 但你们知道谁被指控了吗？

sentences.en: We were.
sentences.zh: 是我们。

sentences.en: They've actually charged us with felonies for daring to defend our home.
sentences.zh: 他们竟然因为我们敢于保卫家园而指控我们犯有重罪。

sentences.en: And one of the things that was most striking to me about their segment was that, in contrast to a lot of the other politicians who spoke, with really sort of forceful rhetoric,
sentences.zh: 关于他们的环节，最让我印象深刻的一点是，与许多发表强硬言论的政客相比，

sentences.en: they had this calming presence.
sentences.zh: 他们有一种冷静的存在感。

sentences.en: What you saw happen to us could just as easily happen to any of you who are watching from quiet neighborhoods around our country.
sentences.zh: 你们看到发生在我们身上的事，同样可能发生在你们任何一位从全国各地安静社区观看节目的人身上。

sentences.en: And that's what we want to speak to you about tonight.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今晚想和你们谈论的。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Even as they were saying, you need to worry about mobs coming for you in your quiet neighborhood around the country.
sentences.zh: 即使他们当时说，你们需要担心暴民来到你们全国各地的安静社区。

sentences.en: And it is Patricia McCloskey who specifically tells us...
sentences.zh: 正是帕特里夏·麦克洛斯基明确告诉我们……

sentences.en: They're not satisfied with spreading the chaos and violence into our communities.
sentences.zh: 他们不满足于将混乱和暴力蔓延到我们的社区。

sentences.en: Not only do Democrats want to spread chaos into the suburbs...
sentences.zh: 民主党人不仅想把混乱蔓延到郊区……

sentences.en: They want to abolish the suburbs altogether by ending single-family home zoning.
sentences.zh: 他们还想通过结束独栋住宅分区来彻底废除郊区。

sentences.en: This forestry zoning would bring crime, lawlessness, and low-quality apartments into now-thriving suburban neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 这种森林分区将给现在繁荣的郊区社区带来犯罪、无法无天和低质量的公寓。

sentences.en: They want to make it such that you can't have sort of your nice, quiet suburban neighborhood full of single-family houses.
sentences.zh: 他们想让你无法拥有那种充满独栋住宅的、美好安静的郊区社区。

sentences.en: The Democrats have brought us nothing but destruction.
sentences.zh: 民主党人除了破坏什么也没带给我们。

sentences.en: When we don't have basic safety and security in our communities, we'll never be free to build a brighter future for ourselves, for our children, or for our country.
sentences.zh: 当我们社区没有基本的安全保障时，我们将永远无法自由地为我们自己、为我们的孩子或为我们的国家建设更美好的未来。

sentences.en: That's what's at stake in this election.
sentences.zh: 这就是这次选举所面临的利害关系。

sentences.en: And that's why we must re-elect Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们必须重新选举唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: So here again, as in 1968, we have a focus on housing regulations as a way of talking about this.
sentences.zh: 所以在这里，就像1968年一样，我们关注住房法规，以此作为谈论这个问题的方式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: When she says that the Democrats want to abolish the suburbs, she is alluding to a piece of the 1968 Fair Housing Act.
sentences.zh: 当她说民主党人想要废除郊区时，她是在影射1968年《公平住房法》的一部分。

sentences.en: Again, we're coming back to 1968, that the Obama administration had adopted a rule trying to encourage communities all over the country, not just the suburbs,
sentences.zh: 我们又回到了1968年，奥巴马政府曾采纳了一项规则，试图鼓励全国各地的社区，不仅仅是郊区，

sentences.en: to embrace integration.
sentences.zh: 去拥抱融合。

sentences.en: And earlier this summer, the Trump administration rolled back that rule, and Trump announced that the suburban housewives of America should be thrilled that I have done this.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天早些时候，特朗普政府撤销了该规则，特朗普宣布美国的郊区家庭主妇应该为我所做的感到高兴。

sentences.en: And your very quality of life, you will not have control over it.
sentences.zh: 而你们的生活质量，你们将无法控制它。

sentences.en: The federal government will come in and remake your neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府会介入并重塑你们的社区。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: The other parallel that fell most over to me, Emily, was this recurring message that all this talk, as in 1968, is not raciSt.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，另一个让我感触最深的相似之处是，这种反复出现的信息，即所有这些言论，正如1968年一样，并不是种族主义。

sentences.en: But in this case, it wasn't the Republican nominee.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，这不是共和党候选人说的。

sentences.en: It wasn't Donald Trump saying this.
sentences.zh: 不是唐纳德·特朗普说的。

sentences.en: It was Republicans of color.
sentences.zh: 而是有色人种的共和党人。

sentences.en: It was, for example, Kim Klasik.
sentences.zh: 例如，金·克拉西克。

sentences.en: My name is Kim Klasik, and I'm running for Congress in Maryland's 7th District.
sentences.zh: 我叫金·克拉西克，我正在竞选马里兰州第七选区的国会议员。

sentences.en: A black woman running for Congress in Baltimore, and she's running on a message that Democrats have let Baltimore down.
sentences.zh: 一位在巴尔的摩竞选国会议员的黑人女性，她的竞选信息是民主党人让巴尔的摩失望了。

sentences.en: Sadly, the same cycle of decay exists in many of America's Democrat-run cities.
sentences.zh: 可悲的是，同样的衰落循环存在于许多由民主党管理的美国城市中。

sentences.en: And yet the Democrats still assume that black people will vote for them, no matter how much they let us down and take us for granted.
sentences.zh: 然而，民主党人仍然认为黑人会投票给他们，无论他们让我们失望多少次，无论他们如何把我们视为理所当然。

sentences.en: We're sick of it.
sentences.zh: 我们受够了。

sentences.en: We're not going to take it anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们再也不会忍受了。

sentences.en: And we also heard a similar message from Tim Scott.
sentences.zh: 我们也从蒂姆·斯科特那里听到了类似的信息。

sentences.en: We live in a world that only wants you to believe in the bad news, racially, economically, and culturally polarizing news.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个只希望你相信坏消息的世界里，那些在种族、经济和文化上具有两极分化色彩的新闻。

sentences.en: The truth is, our nation's arc always bends back towards fairness.
sentences.zh: 事实是，我们国家的弧线总是向着公平回归。

sentences.en: A black senator from South Carolina and from Nikki Haley.
sentences.zh: 一位来自南卡罗来纳州的黑人参议员，还有妮基·黑利。

sentences.en: In much of the Democratic Party, it's now fashionable to say that America is raciSt.
sentences.zh: 在民主党的大部分人中，现在流行说美国是种族主义国家。

sentences.en: That is a lie.
sentences.zh: 那是谎言。

sentences.en: America is not a racist country.
sentences.zh: 美国不是一个种族主义国家。

sentences.en: This is personal for me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说是私人的事。

sentences.en: Who is of Indian descent and who was Trump's ambassador to the United Nations.
sentences.zh: 她是印度裔，曾担任特朗普的驻联合国大使。

sentences.en: Yeah, we also heard something similar from Herschel Walker, who is the former football player who has had this very long-running,
sentences.zh: 是的，我们也从赫歇尔·沃克那里听到了类似的话，他是前橄榄球运动员，与唐纳德·特朗普有着非常长期的、

sentences.en: almost four-decade-long relationship with Donald Trump, who is also African-American and effectively said...
sentences.zh: 长达近四十年的关系，他也是非裔美国人，他实际上说……

sentences.en: It hurt my soul to hear the terrible names that people call Donald.
sentences.zh: 听到人们给唐纳德起的那些可怕的名字，我的灵魂感到痛苦。

sentences.en: The worst one is raciSt.
sentences.zh: 最糟糕的一个是种族主义者。

sentences.en: I take it as a personal insult that people would think I've had a 37-year friendship with a raciSt.
sentences.zh: 人们认为我和一个种族主义者有37年的友谊，我对此感到个人侮辱。

sentences.en: People who think that don't know what they're talking about.
sentences.zh: 有这种想法的人根本不知道他们在说什么。

sentences.en: You know, I am offended by the idea that anyone would think that I have been friends with a racist for the last 37 years.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，有人认为我和一个种族主义者做了37年的朋友，这种想法让我感到被冒犯了。

sentences.en: Just because someone loves and respects the flag, our national anthem, and our country, doesn't mean they don't care about social justice.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为有人热爱并尊重国旗、国歌和我们的国家，并不意味着他们不关心社会正义。

sentences.en: I care about all of those things.
sentences.zh: 我关心所有这些事情。

sentences.en: So does Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普也是如此。

sentences.en: So, Emily, from Trump's point of view, this strategy would seem to have a very solid track record.
sentences.zh: 那么，艾米丽，从特朗普的角度来看，这一策略似乎有着非常稳固的成功记录。

sentences.en: So is there any reason to think that it would not work now, in 2020?
sentences.zh: 那么，有什么理由认为它在2020年的今天行不通呢？

sentences.en: One big reason is that the suburbs themselves have changed dramatically since the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 一个重要的原因是，自20世纪60年代以来，郊区本身已经发生了巨大的变化。

sentences.en: The women who live in the suburbs today are much more racially diverse.
sentences.zh: 如今居住在郊区的女性在种族上更加多元化。

sentences.en: They're more economically diverse.
sentences.zh: 她们在经济上也更加多元化。

sentences.en: When we talk about suburban voters in suburbia today, it is much less clear exactly who we're talking about,
sentences.zh: 当我们今天谈论郊区选民时，我们到底在谈论谁，这一点已经变得模糊多了，

sentences.en: because it's no longer just middle-class and upper-income white voters who are living in these communities.
sentences.zh: 因为居住在这些社区的不再仅仅是中产阶级和高收入的白人选民。

sentences.en: There's poverty in these communities.
sentences.zh: 这些社区里也存在贫困。

sentences.en: There are immigrant communities who live in the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 郊区也有移民社区。

sentences.en: And so this is not the voting bloc that Richard Nixon was speaking to in 1968, or the voting bloc that it seems like Donald Trump has in mind.
sentences.zh: 所以，这并不是理查德·尼克松在1968年所针对的选民群体，也不是唐纳德·特朗普心目中想的那种选民群体。

sentences.en: But the other reason why I think we should be really skeptical is that we see in polling data
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们应该保持高度怀疑的另一个原因是，我们从民调数据中看到，

sentences.en: that voters in the suburbs today, majorities of them are supportive of the Black Lives Matter movement.
sentences.zh: 如今的郊区选民中，大多数人支持“黑人的命也是命”运动。

sentences.en: They're supportive of these protests.
sentences.zh: 他们支持这些抗议活动。

sentences.en: They are even participating in these protests.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至亲自参与了这些抗议。

sentences.en: And so they're really sort of not necessarily receptive to the issues that Trump is trying to elevate,
sentences.zh: 所以，他们并不一定会被特朗普试图提升的议题所打动，

sentences.en: but he's also trying to get them to focus on a set of issues which are not their primary concern right now.
sentences.zh: 而且他试图让他们关注的一系列议题，并非他们目前最关心的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, between the pandemic and the collapse of the economy and millions of Americans losing their health care as a result of that,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在疫情和经济崩溃，以及数百万美国人因此失去医疗保险的情况下，

sentences.en: you know, those are the three issues that really sit at the top of suburban voters and female voters' concerns when we ask them what they're concerned about right now.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们询问郊区选民和女性选民目前最关心什么时，这三个问题确实位居她们关注点的前列。

sentences.en: But it does seem like there might be an X factor here that Donald Trump has been priming suburban voters for.
sentences.zh: 但似乎确实存在一个不确定因素，而唐纳德·特朗普一直在为郊区选民做这方面的心理铺垫。

sentences.en: And an example of that would be what's going on right now in Wisconsin,
sentences.zh: 一个例子就是威斯康星州目前正在发生的事情，

sentences.en: where there are protests against the shooting of a Black man, Jacob Blake,
sentences.zh: 那里发生了针对黑人雅各布·布莱克被枪击事件的抗议活动，

sentences.en: and those protests have turned into fires and looting on top of the situation that we have had in cities like Portland.
sentences.zh: 除了波特兰等城市已经出现的情况外，这些抗议活动还演变成了纵火和抢劫。

sentences.en: And could it be that the polling that you're referring to is not quite up to date
sentences.zh: 有没有可能你提到的民调结果还不够及时，

sentences.en: and that there may be voters who hear the president talking at this convention and thinking to themselves, I do support Black Lives Matter, but I don't support this.
sentences.zh: 而且可能有些选民在这次大会上听到总统的讲话后会想：我确实支持“黑人的命也是命”，但我不支持这种行为。

sentences.en: I don't support what I'm seeing on my television screen in places like Kenosha, Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 我不支持我在电视屏幕上看到的发生在威斯康星州基诺沙等地的事情。

sentences.en: I think the biggest unknown over the next two months, which could play to the president's advantage, is that there will be more Kenosha's.
sentences.zh: 我认为未来两个月最大的未知数，也是可能对总统有利的一点，就是还会出现更多的“基诺沙事件”。

sentences.en: And I think we don't know at this point how more scenes like that might change or erode public opinion about these issues in the months to come.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，在接下来的几个月里，更多类似的场景会如何改变或侵蚀公众对这些议题的看法，我们目前还不得而知。

sentences.en: But I think that in order for this strategy to work for Trump, suburban women need to not only become concerned about these scenes,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，要让这一策略对特朗普奏效，郊区女性不仅需要对这些场景感到担忧，

sentences.en: but they have to believe that their own neighborhoods are threatened in this moment.
sentences.zh: 她们还必须相信自己的社区在这一刻受到了威胁。

sentences.en: And the question is, will suburban voters really see it that way in 2020?
sentences.zh: 问题是，郊区选民在2020年真的会那样看吗？

sentences.en: Or has simply too much changed since 1968?
sentences.zh: 还是说自1968年以来，一切都已经发生了太大的变化？

sentences.en: Emily, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Yeah, thanks for the conversation.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你的交流。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: I want to acknowledge the fact that since March, our lives have changed drastically.
sentences.zh: 我想承认这样一个事实，自三月以来，我们的生活发生了翻天覆地的变化。

sentences.en: The invisible enemy, COVID-19, swept across our beautiful country and impacted all of us.
sentences.zh: 隐形的敌人——新冠病毒席卷了我们美丽的国家，影响了我们所有人。

sentences.en: On the second night of the Republican National Convention,
sentences.zh: 在共和党全国代表大会的第二晚，

sentences.en: First Lady Melania Trump confronted a topic that has been largely missing from the proceedings so far, the painful impact of the coronavirus pandemic.
sentences.zh: 第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普谈到了一个到目前为止在会议中基本被忽略的话题：新冠疫情带来的痛苦影响。

sentences.en: My deepest sympathy goes out to everyone who has lost a loved one.
sentences.zh: 我向所有失去亲人的人表示最深切的同情。

sentences.en: And my prayers are with those who are ill or suffering.
sentences.zh: 我的祈祷与那些生病或受苦的人同在。

sentences.en: I know many people are anxious and some feel helpless.
sentences.zh: 我知道许多人感到焦虑，有些人感到无助。

sentences.en: I want you to know you're not alone.
sentences.zh: 我想让你们知道，你们并不孤单。

sentences.en: The First Lady focused much of her speech on appealing to women and mothers by seeking to portray her husband as their protector.
sentences.zh: 第一夫人将演讲的大部分内容集中在吸引女性和母亲上，试图将她的丈夫描绘成她们的保护者。

sentences.en: To mothers and parents everywhere, you are warriors.
sentences.zh: 致各地的母亲和父母们，你们是战士。

sentences.en: In my husband, you have a president who will not stop fighting for you and your families.
sentences.zh: 在我的丈夫身上，你们拥有了一位会为你们和你们的家庭不断抗争的总统。

sentences.en: I see how hard he works each day and night.
sentences.zh: 我看到了他每天每夜工作得有多么努力。

sentences.en: And despite the unprecedented attacks from the media and opposition, he will not give up.
sentences.zh: 尽管来自媒体和反对派的攻击前所未有，但他绝不会放弃。

sentences.en: In fact, if you tell him he cannot be done, he just works harder.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你告诉他某件事做不到，他只会更加努力。

sentences.en: And on Tuesday, in a sign of the pandemic's ongoing economic toll,
sentences.zh: 周二，作为疫情持续造成经济损失的一个迹象，

sentences.en: American Airlines said it would furlough 19,000 workers when its federal financial aid, which totaled nearly $6 billion, comes to an end this fall.
sentences.zh: 美国航空表示，当其总额近60亿美元的联邦财政援助在今年秋季到期时，将不得不让1.9万名员工休无薪假。

sentences.en: By October, the airline will have reduced its workforce by 30 percent.
sentences.zh: 到十月份，该航空公司的员工人数将减少30%。

sentences.en: Americans' rivals, Delta and United, say that they too may need to cut jobs this fall.
sentences.zh: 美国航空的竞争对手达美航空和联合航空也表示，他们今年秋季可能也需要裁员。

sentences.en: The announcements are likely to increase pressure on Congress to pass new economic relief, something that lawmakers have been unable to do for weeks.
sentences.zh: 这些公告可能会增加国会通过新经济救助计划的压力，而这正是立法者们几周来一直未能做到的。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台受到严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，该党就陷入了一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《Metro》的最新一期节目中，我和莎拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在你获取播客的任何平台收听。

sentences.en: come here.
sentences.zh: 过来。

sentences.en: It has gotten a walk-you
sentences.zh: 它已经变成了一个让你...

sentences.en: Let's monitor.
sentences.zh: 让我们监控一下。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
